excerpt: For incoming sensory pathways, the source states that adding or removing multiple segregated incoming pathways does not change the composition of the main complex and causes little change in Φ; the larger complex including those pathways has low Φ because it is limited by effective information between each afferent pathway and its port-in. A parallel point is made for outgoing pathways and port-out elements.
overview: This model constraint explains how unconscious processes can influence conscious contents without being constituents of consciousness. Inputs and outputs can be causally important for what a conscious complex does or receives, yet fail to add dimensions to the experience if they are informationally segregated from the main complex. The scope is boundary-setting: it distinguishes modulation and access from direct phenomenological contribution.
title: Ports Stay Outside Complex
